idea: Shape every TSP/DEVL decision explanation to Miller's four properties: contrastive (why grant priority rather than not), selected (one or two causes, not all inputs), social/audience-specific, post hoc. Plus three stakeholder views: developer (debug), regulator/auditor (justification), end user (short).
does: Builds a contrastive explanation record for a TSP/DEVL decision: chosen action vs the best alternative, with the top 1-2 deciding factors (e.g. bus delay s, queue on the conflicting phase) and a short/long version per audience.
inputs: agent decision log entry (request, state snapshot, chosen action), alternative action counterfactual outcome
notes: Prompt-level change; cheap. Counterfactual alt could come from a cloned headless run.

idea: Taxonomy of explanation techniques: scope (global/local), stage (intrinsic/post hoc), model-agnostic vs specific; local instance-level justification is what regulation needs. Suggests logging each agent decision as a local, intrinsic rule-trace.
does: Persistent per-decision audit trail (inputs, rule/LLM rationale, outcome) exportable in results workbook for after-the-fact review.
notes: Extends TSP telemetry to DEVL and assistant tool choices.

idea: Three-part framework: controller (maps environment e to action a in finite set A), a safety-regulatory compliance component srC that runs N safety tests against the controller and requires a pass threshold (e.g. 90%), and an XAI component giving textual justification for every action. Apply to TSP/DEVL agents: a fixed battery of scenario invariants (never blocks an emergency vehicle's route, never exceeds a max red extension, never starves a phase) run headless against an agent before it is trusted.
does: Runs a scenario battery headless with an LLM agent in the loop, checks safety invariants per run, reports pass rate vs threshold and the failing scenario with its decision trace.
inputs: agent config, scenario list (built by build_scenario), invariants (max starvation s, EV blocked s, red extension cap)
outputs: pass-rate table, failures with decision logs
notes: Invariants list from the chapter: no block of emergency route, no running red, obey speed limit, takeover fallback when automation fails.

idea: After a failure (collision-like event, gridlock, EV delayed) produce a post-incident report asking: was the controller's fault, or road conditions/other participants; list chosen action, alternatives and residual risk of each (ISO 26262 style evidence-based rationale).
does: For a flagged event in a run, pulls the agent decisions in the preceding window and reports decision, rationale, residual risk, and whether a no-agent baseline would have avoided it.
inputs: run results, decision log, event time
notes: Counterfactual via re-run with same seed minus the agent action.

idea: Interpretable short-term flow prediction: spatiotemporal model that extracts which upstream road segments contribute most to a target road's next state; LSTM attention weights as explanations.
does: For a congested road, rank upstream roads by lagged correlation/regression coefficient with its flow and report them as the likely causes.
inputs: per-road flow/speed time series from results
notes: Stdlib least squares only; survey-level source.

idea: Model-based planning is naturally explainable: before acting, roll the world model forward for each candidate action and show predicted state and reward trajectory; the explanation is the comparison of predicted outcomes. For TSP/DEVL, fork the simulation state, run each option (grant / deny / extend green N s) for a short horizon, and quote predicted bus delay, cross-street queue and EV travel time in the decision.
does: Counterfactual short-horizon rollouts of candidate TSP/DEVL actions from a snapshot of the live run; returns per-action predicted KPIs that the LLM agent uses to choose and to justify.
inputs: Frame/state snapshot, candidate actions, horizon s, seed
outputs: table action -> predicted bus delay, person-delay, queue lengths
notes: Needs a deep-copyable sim state; the headless runner exists. Also gives the decision deadline problem a cheap answer for batch runs.

idea: Question-driven hierarchy: store each decision as a Q/A pair (Why did the signal hold green? Because bus B12 was 40 s late and the cross queue was short) and let the assistant answer follow-up temporal questions about any past decision.
does: Assistant tool that, given a time and junction/vehicle, returns the stored decision Q&A and the state at that moment, supporting follow-up questions.
outputs: decision record with Q/A text and state

idea: Decisions with different risk levels: pure max-reward acting can miss the best policy; make agent prompts state a risk level (e.g. EV in motion = low risk tolerance, no gambles on cross-street starvation).
does: Adds a risk tier to the agent prompt per request type.

idea: Seasonal exponential smoothing (additive Holt-Winters without trend: L(t)=alpha(Y(t)-S(t-s))+(1-alpha)L(t-1); S(t)=gamma(Y(t)-L(t))+(1-gamma)S(t-s); forecast Y^(t+k)=L(t)+S(t+k-s)) fitted on a baseline period, forecast over the study period, then days/intervals above the forecast upper limit are flagged as abnormal; goodness of fit by RMSE, MAPE, Ljung-Box Q on residuals (p>0.05 = random residuals).
does: Fits a seasonal smoothing baseline to a per-interval KPI (arrivals, mean speed, queue) from baseline runs, and flags intervals in a test run that exceed the forecast band; reports fit quality.
inputs: KPI time series from results (baseline runs, season length e.g. 24 h of 15-min bins), test series
outputs: forecast with upper limit, flagged intervals, RMSE/MAPE/Ljung-Box
notes: All stdlib. Can also give a before/after (what-if) effect estimate: observed minus counterfactual forecast, which the chapter uses for COVID impact.

idea: Exhaustive CHAID decision tree (chi-square split, merging categories until two super-categories, p-value to choose the split variable, 70/30 train-test) to rank which categorical factors (time of day, road user, age) segment severe outcomes; tree read directly as rules.
does: Chi-square tree over per-vehicle or per-trip records (type, origin, hour band, route) to show which factors separate long-delay or stopped-often trips.
inputs: per-vehicle trip records from results workbook, outcome class (e.g. delay tercile)
outputs: readable rule tree with counts and p-values
notes: Needs per-vehicle trip times (not exact today per not_built).

idea: Reward decomposition and reward-difference explanation: split an agent's utility into named semantic components (bus delay saved, cross-street delay added, EV time, stops) and explain a choice by the component-wise difference between chosen action and the best alternative, rather than a single score. Caveat from the survey: single-step decomposition ignores future behaviour, so combine with a lookahead.
does: For each TSP/DEVL request computes a fixed vector of person-delay components per candidate action (from lookahead rollout or a closed-form estimate) and returns the per-component difference chosen vs alternative.
inputs: candidate actions, per-component estimator, state snapshot
outputs: component table and one-line contrast ('chose X: bus -18 s, cross +9 s, net -9 s')
cite: Ch 5 s5.4.2 (reward decomposition, reward difference explanations)
notes: Pairs with lookahead_rollout. Components are person-weighted using vehicle occupancy already in ACMS.

idea: Contrastive explanations by a policy foil: compare the trajectory under the agent's policy with the trajectory under a foil (the alternative the user expected), e.g. 'why not give the bus priority?'. Also risk-of-state explanation using the next n states.
does: Answers a user why-not question by simulating the foil action from the same snapshot and presenting both outcome trajectories.
inputs: decision time, junction, foil action named by user

idea: Causal-confusion test: before deployment, build alternative environments from critical states and compare the policy against one that sees only a subset of features; plus action-influence graph (features as nodes, actions as edges) for minimal sufficient explanations. Practical form for LLM agents: occlusion test, drop or perturb each prompt input (queue length, bus lateness, EV distance) and re-ask; inputs whose removal flips the decision are the decisive ones.
does: Re-queries the agent with each input feature perturbed or removed on a sample of recorded decisions and reports flip rates per feature, exposing spurious reliance.
inputs: recorded agent requests (state dicts), agent callable
outputs: per-feature flip rate, list of decisions that depend on one feature only
cite: Ch 5 s5.4.5 (action influence graphs, causal confusion), s5.4.7 saliency for traffic signal control
notes: Model-agnostic like LIME; cost is extra LLM calls, so run on a sample and with local Ollama.

idea: ZORRO-style perturbation importance per intersection: for a given signal plan, replace one junction's offset by a random value in 0..cycle-1, re-evaluate total waiting at red, fidelity = absolute % change from the original; mean over many sampled plans is that junction's importance. Chapter shows the same ranking as Shapley values (permutation sampling, sample size 10 x features) and that importance differs near local optima vs random plans.
does: Ranks signalised junctions by how much randomising their offset (or green split) changes network red-wait/delay, to show where coordination matters and where timing tuning is wasted.
inputs: network with plan, N sampled perturbations per junction, short headless run each, seeds
outputs: table junction -> mean abs % change in total red wait / delay, with CI
existing: partial: TRANSYT and Synchro offsets (optimise, never diagnose sensitivity)
notes: Use real headless runs instead of the book's GNN surrogate; paired seeds per perturbation. Metric used in book: total waiting time at red over 10 min. Offsets in 0..119 with red 62 s/green 58 s.

idea: Surrogate metamodel of the simulator: train on ~1e5 simulated pairs (offset vector -> total red wait), architecture mirrors the road graph (neurons = intersections/segments, links only where roads connect), then use it as the evaluator inside a genetic algorithm to find offsets in seconds instead of simulating each candidate.
does: Builds a cheap regression surrogate (e.g. additive per-junction plus neighbour-pair terms fitted by least squares on sampled headless runs) and runs a GA over offsets with it, validating the best few in the true sim.
inputs: network, N sampled offset vectors with simulated total red wait, GA settings
outputs: best offset vector, surrogate error (MAPE), validation run result
existing: partial: TRANSYT/Synchro offline optimisation (analytic, not simulator-in-the-loop)
cite: Ch 7 s7.2 (surrogate GNN, Warsaw districts 11/21/42 junctions)
notes: No numpy: a sparse linear/pairwise surrogate in stdlib is feasible; the GNN is not. Book's MAPE on test set was the selection criterion.

idea: Reconstruct missing detector counts of a station from nearby stations by OLS (R2 0.63-0.96) and SARIMA (best, seasonal weekly cycle); remove outliers by the interquartile range before fitting; STL decomposition shows trend/season/residual.
does: For imported real counts (to calibrate OD demand), fills gaps from neighbouring stations with least squares and drops IQR outliers.
notes: ACMS has no real-count import yet; only useful if calibration from counts is added.

idea: Per-trip kinematic features from successive logs: speed V=d/dT, acceleration A=dV/dT, jerk J=dA/dT, bearing rate; trip statistics (mean, median, std, 10/25/75/90th percentiles, CV, skew, kurtosis) plus stop rate and velocity-change rate, with thresholds so that congested driving is told apart from walking. As simulation KPIs: stops per km, jerk RMS (comfort), speed percentiles and CV per vehicle type or road.
does: Computes stop rate, jerk and speed-distribution statistics from the per-vehicle samples already recorded, to compare scenarios on smoothness and stop-and-go, not only mean delay.
inputs: per-vehicle position/speed samples (5 s) from results
outputs: KPI table per vehicle type / road / scenario
existing: partial: results KPIs (throughput, delay); no stop rate/jerk
cite: Ch 10 s10.3.2 Eq 10.1, advanced travel features
notes: 5 s sampling is too coarse for jerk; stop rate and percentiles are fine. Jerk would need physics-step logging.

idea: Distributed predictors voting with recorded predictions and explanations (blockchain-style immutable audit trail with smart-contract aggregation); simple stdlib form is a hash-chained append-only decision log plus majority vote of several LLM agents (e.g. Jev and Laya) for TSP requests.
does: Asks two or more agents the same TSP/DEVL question, aggregates by vote or confidence, and logs each answer with a hash chain so a run's decisions are tamper-evident.
outputs: aggregated decision, disagreement flag, hashed log
notes: Disagreement between agents is itself a useful diagnostic. Conceptual chapter, no algorithm.
